CONTEXT: This review is from the perspective of someone who started playing "Risk of Rain 2" before knowing about "Risk of Rain Returns" as well as the original "Risk of Rain" Returns is based off of. 
Make of that what you will.

   This here is a great action rogue-like with a lot of emphasis on positioning related to the environment, enemies, your attacks/skills and what the little bean pixels in the middle of your screen that you may call your avatar can do.
I find this game's CORE loop to be akin to the spectacle fights of a "Monster Hunter" game. Where you try to find the most available "in the moment" opportunity you can achieve rather than "the best one always", if that makes any sense ha ha!
   You can not control where your characters can "shoot" the way most of us, newcomers, would think of: with a mouse(?) No! Instead it is based of whatever the skill itself says so coupled to where your character is either: currently facing, is mid-air or not, the current movement input or if its standing still. And while that can (as it certainly did for me) come of as a turn-off at first, this actually pairs really well with the emphasis on POSITIONING! While I still would love for some more customization/accessibility for the aiming aspect, its more of a "wishful" thinking rather than a fair complain. XD
   That leads me to my real complaint to this one game as a Rogue-Like. The lack of agency in the BUILDING aspects of each run I have. By that I mean: The gave does not give me as a player enough tools/ways of "manipulating the RNG" like in games such as "The Binding of Isaac" or "Noita". And while that in a way can be a boon for players more interested in the action of RORR rather than having to break the flow of combat, I wish it would've implemented elements from the sequel, such as Scrappers and Printers found around the levels. And yes, I am aware of Drifter, I just wish I could do some of the same things she can while playing other characters. '--

   Overall this is a game with a lot of interesting ideas, concepts and good game design practices that can still be used as references to future games, to any game developers out there looking for inspiration. While its controls can seem odd at first, their pair perfectly with everything this game is about. 

   "Can't wait to Risk the hell out of my life when the Rain of Petrichor V Returns"
